title: Can we all just collectively agree that it is not the AI but the people?
author: frindenolms
selftext:
a dev could literally make an ugly game without AI but would still get upvoted 2k by a community from r/indiedev. *however* if that person did infact made it with AI, they're going to blame the AI and absolutely trash the game. 

now a dev could literally make a game with a good *story line,* *good art style,* *good music,* and so on and so forth. if they admitted that they used AI, they're going to be downvoted and the anti-AI freaks would over-analyze the game to find mistakes and, *yet again* blame the AI. 

someone would absolutely find this logical but are going to say ''anything made by AI is a slop *because it destroys the environment''* while actively breathing and supporting companies that *takes more earthly resources.* 

×××× i'm 17 yrs old and a lot of my friends and people that i know are becoming anti-AI. a funny thing happened to me, when we were calculating something, my friend used a calculator and i used AI. she reprimanded me for using AI and she said that calculating it is easy so why use AI in the first place. i told her that she used a calculator yet i didn't say anything. she just simply said atleast *it isn't AI.*

i remember reading an article that calculators were once debated by school mathematicians and some. they said that they fear newer generations would become far more illiterate if calculators were introduced to schools. 

this is probably why i overachieve. i have been using AI since chatgpt was first released. a lot of noise generalizing how it will make people become far more illiterate. so i overachieve too much with AI because i want to prove them wrong. if any sane soul ever dares to speak that anyone can do it with AI, i'm going to slap them the $11k usd i made in a span of 21 days with the help of AI and tell them to do it. 

but i realize you can't convince them. if you become dumber they blame it to AI tech. if you don't, they're going to say it's because of AI so i'm cheating. 🤡  

AI tech needs to be regulated, yes i do agree. it is not purely good and bad. there are some pessimists and optimists. thankyou 💌

replies.author: Dicethrower
replies.body:
>Cognitive Atrophy is a something even seasoned experienced developer have raised as a concern

As a seasoned experienced developer I see many seasoned experienced developers coping hard with the changes right now, so I'm not shocked they would say this.

There have always been 2 types of developers in this industry. Those that love the process of programming and have always looked at games as a fun way to apply it, and those that love making and shipping games and learned the process of programming so they would be good at it. The former are struggling right now because the fun thing they want to apply their process to no longer wants it. The latter are celebrating because the fun part has become easier.

So "cognitive atrophy" is the kind of thing the former would come up with to argue their process is still relevant, and that using and/or relying on AI will make them less relevant somehow. It's a transparent and desperate attempt to get people to slow down and/or reverse.

I've been a gamedev for +15y and if anything I'm applying my critical thinking skills more than ever. What we used to do during a 2 week sprint is now done in a day, if not a few hours. That means more time spending on thinking, designing, discovering, etc. Less time mindlessly grinding away writing/testing/fixing code where you already know what you want but you just have to do it.

replies.author: justanotherguy28
replies.body:
Some probably are using it a crutch and a scapegoat. That said, You’re missing the contextual application and focusing on a single aspect whilst also ignoring other anthropological data. New technology does affect previously common observable traits.   
  
As more instant information storage access became available, recorded average memory weighting dropped because it moved to a more defunct skill. *Example is telephone numbers*. It isn’t an instant change, sometimes a few years, maybe a generation.   
  
New technology can also affect physical traits not just cognitive. Due to many children raised from infants utilising screen devices close to their eyes this is causing an increase in myopic vision.  
  
To think humans won’t adjust, accommodate, or become dependent on a new technology is just ignoring the data.

\> a dev could literally make an ugly game without AI but would still get upvoted 2k by a community from [r/indiedev](https://www.reddit.com/r/indiedev/). *however* if that person did infact made it with AI, they're going to blame the AI and absolutely trash the game.

I'm actually anti AI for some things, especially education, Claude is fantastic and I use it all the time, but I don't learn stuff (except about AI) and I worry that I am getting too willing to turn to AI to find the answer instead of figuring it out myself. Yeah you could use it as a calculator, but I think the energy efficiency of both methods would be a black mark for AI. On the flip side I couldn't have accomplished some major things this year without it, it got me over hurdles that would have stymied me before, and they were in areas I did not want to be an expert in.

I am torn on AI in Art, I know the AI is only as good as it is because it has sampled everyones art, and remixed it without attribution. However thats what human artists do too, in a more organic way, we all stand on the shoulder of those before us. It is the discrepency in how fast AI builds it's skill, thousands of hours of practice handed to non expert people as a gift. It affects artists badly, and that makes me sad as an artist. It will affect more professions and hobbies monetarily in time.

These days I have decided to look upon it as a tool, for development, for art, for projects. I am unsure if it will ever let me be financially secure making games and art, but I am attempting to go that way anyway.

comments.author: RPGGod
comments.body:
So it's an interesting query I've had quite a bit of experience in gamedev before the AI wave came about. 

Let me preface this by saying I think the frontier models easily surpass my own knowledge and I know very few engineers who could out code a focused AI. They are simply getting to specialized for the tasks. However I think the mistake people make isn't necessarily that AI games are slop, it's the devs that use them one shot something and call it a perfection. Games take a lot, beyond what you can imagine. You have performance, the feel of the gameplay, and underlying design. AI cannot do these, it is going to make some assumptions that are just plain wrong. As for coding it won't just choose the optimal path, even trying to guide it sometimes it attempts to derail and take the easy path.

You have to understand what it's doing, I take any work I do with AI as it's a submission/pr from a junior dev. I look it over and correct the bad parts
